This Widebody Lamborghini Temerario Looks Like a Gentleman’s Supercar
13 photos
Photo: Instagram | 1016industries
Did you somehow think that we have covered the Lamborghini Temerario so extensively that there is nothing more to be said about it? Well, that may be partially true, but that does not mean that we cannot put the spotlight on the occasional example that deserves to celebrate its 15 minutes of online fame.
Speaking of that, the one pictured above definitely fits the bill, as it certainly looks a lot more exciting than the stock one. One of the first things that makes it stand out compared to the standard Temerarios is the satin green look. The color is said to be the OEM Verde Hydra Matte, and was applied to all body panels, making this machine look like a veritable gentleman’s supercar, as mentioned in the title.
If you look at the pictures shared in the gallery, then you will see that there are also some black details here and there. However, these do not provide that much contrast, but the bronze wheels do. These feature a turbine-like design, spin around the orange brake calipers, and have been shod in sticky rubber from Michelin. The alloys are said to be a new addition to the 1016 Industries portfolio, and they are definitely not the only thing to have come from the quoted tuner when it comes to the Lamborghini Temerario in question.
That’s because the supercar also benefits from their 1016 Vision Widebody Kit, which makes it look a lot more aggressive. Things such as the front fender attachments, the add-ons on the sides of the OEM front bumper, and the chin spoiler are new, and as you can clearly see, so is the front hood with its vented design close to the windscreen. The side skirts are also new, and they feature some blades at the rear, thus mirroring the look of the splitter.
Photo: Instagram | 1016industries Further back, this Lamborghini Temerario features new trim surrounding the rear air intakes on the outer edges. The wing that rests on the rear deck is also new, and so is the diffuser, complete with its extra brake light mounted in the middle. The add-ons that are part of the tuner’s widebody kit have been made of carbon fiber, and they sport a naked look here, thus making the supercar appear even more aggressive.
Care to talk about the interior? Well, so do we, but unfortunately, it hasn’t opened up to the camera in the images that @1016industries shared on Instagram earlier this week. Thus, it is likely that the cabin hasn’t been modified, and from what we can see by zooming in through the windows in certain pictures, it appears to be mostly black, though there should be some contrasting elements on deck. That’s what we think, anyway.
The enhanced look of this particular Lamborghini Temerario is not joined by a power boost, or if it is, then 1016 Industries hasn’t said anything about it. But that does not make the supercar any less exciting, because it already dwarfs its predecessors, regardless of the configuration, in terms of power and performance, and for what it’s worth, it gets very close to the larger, punchier, and a lot more expensive Revuelto.
That’s because it has 907 hp (677 kW/920 ps) to play with in total. The Temerario features a 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 engine, assisted by three electric motors. The 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) is a 2.7-second affair, and it will do 213 mph (343 kph) where the road and legislation allow it.
Photo: Instagram | 1016industries If you want to spruce up your weekend drives, or maybe your daily ones if you do not need something more practical for that, with a brand new Lamborghini Temerario , then you will have to pay from close to $400,000 for such a thing. Highly-optioned examples tend to exceed $450,000 and sometimes half a million dollars, so you must have really deep pockets if this model sits at the very top of your shopping list.
The Temerario debuted more than two years ago, and it entered production in 2025. So far, Lamborghini offers a single version of its new-age “baby” supercar, the two-door coupe, but that’s about to change, as the Raging Bull is getting ready to unveil the second body style.
We are talking about the Lamborghini Temerario Spyder , which was recently teased ahead of its official unveiling scheduled for November 18, in Los Angeles. That is when the company will release the full details, including the acceleration time, top speed, and others, while also delving into the characteristics of its power-folding roof that stows away in a special compartment behind the seats.
The open-top model will feature the same powertrain as its fixed-roof sibling, in the same configuration, but due to the added weight, it should be a tiny bit slower.
Now, that does not really matter in this story, as what does is whether you like the tuned Temerario pictured above. So, do you? Because I definitely do! View this post on Instagram A post shared by 1016 Industries (@1016industries)
